subject: Intermittent egress for Hydra private deployment — NAT policy & split‑horizon review
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Hydra Cloud NetOps <netops@hydracloud.com>; A. Priya Sharma <priya@hydracloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent egress failures from hydra-private-1 VPC (observed 07/13-07/14)

Hi Priya / NetOps,

We started seeing intermittent outbound failures from your private deployment (hydra-private-1) late yesterday. Symptoms: HTTP requests to 3rd-party APIs time out for a subset of hosts behind the private NAT gateway; other hosts in the same subnet are fine. Packet counts show retransmits and occasional TCP RSTs from upstream.

Quick facts:
- Affected prefix: 10.200.54.0/24 (app tier)
- Egress path: private NAT -> vendor transit -> internet
- First seen: 2027-07-13 ~22:30 UTC, spike again 2027-07-14 01:10 UTC

I attached a hop trace and a short pcap taken by one of your hosts (hydra-app-05). Can you confirm whether any NAT port rotation, ephemeral port pool limits, or SNAT binding policies changed around 07/13 22:00 UTC? Also, we suspect split‑horizon routing (two possible next-hops for that subnet) — any route-policy changes or blackhole filters applied to the transit nodal set?

Attachments: hydra-hop-trace-20270714.txt (text), hydra-egress-pcap-brief.pcap (pcap snippet)

Next steps I propose:
1) Share NAT binding table snapshot for the NAT gateway covering 07/13-07/14 window
2) Validate whether your transit sees asymmetric routing for these source IPs
3) If NAT port exhaustion looks likely, consider temporary ephemeral-port expansion and let us run a quick smoke test

I'll loop Marissa and Vanessa for routing checks and Vivek for any kernel-level MSS/clamping we should apply.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Platform Reliability — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0197
From: A. Priya Sharma <priya@hydracloud.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Hydra Cloud NetOps <netops@hydracloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent egress failures from hydra-private-1 VPC (observed 07/13-07/14)

Connor — thanks for the quick heads up. We pulled the NAT logs and see a higher than-normal ephemeral port churn starting 07/13 22:24 UTC (matching your window). No deliberate port policy change on our side. Two quick notes:
- We had a transit ACL push at 07/13 21:50 UTC to add deny rules for a compromised prefix; that rollout touched two transit routers but was targeted.
- Our team did a soft reboot of nat-gw-eta at 07/13 22:40 UTC to apply a microcode fix; we thought it was successful.

We'll attach a NAT binding snapshot and will run a routing capture on the transit side in the next 45 minutes. In parallel, can your team provide an app‑side trace (tcpdump + /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range) from hydra-app-05 so we can compare ephemeral ranges?

Priya
NetOps — Hydra Cloud
Attachment: nat-binding-snapshot-07-14.json (redacted)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: A. Priya Sharma <priya@hydracloud.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 10:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent egress failures from hydra-private-1 VPC (observed 07/13-07/14)

Thanks Priya — attaching a short config-diff from our side. Observations from initial triage:
- We see two distinct next-hops for 10.200.54.0/24 in your transit advertisements during the affected window; one path shows a higher RTT and occasional packet reorder.
- The NAT binding snapshot shows ~58k unique mappings near the time of the microcode reboot — which is close to our suspicion of ephemeral-port pressure (default is 65k range, but overhead plus many short-lived connections can saturate).
- A handful of flows show SNAT reuse (different internal sockets mapped to same external port) which correlates with application errors for non-idempotent requests.

Immediate mitigation options we recommend:
1) Expand ip_local_port_range on the affected hosts by 20000 ports (both sides can do this to be safe).
2) Apply a temporary NAT overflow policy: allow NAT gateway to allocate a larger ephemeral pool (we can coordinate a short maintenance window)
3) Pin high-volume services to dedicated egress IPs to avoid sharing with short‑lived bursty clients

I'll create a quick playbook for 1–2 and drop it into Confluence. Vivek — can you confirm whether we should also enable MSS clamping on the private gateway to reduce retransmits given the observed MTU differences?

Attachment: config-diff-connor-20270714.patch

—Marissa
Staff SRE — Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: A. Priya Sharma <priya@hydracloud.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent egress failures from hydra-private-1 VPC (observed 07/13-07/14)

TL;DR: I recommend we enable MSS clamping (set 1360) on the private gateway and increase ephemeral port range on app hosts as a low-risk first pass.

Details:
- The pcap shows repeated ICMP Fragmentation Needed responses in the TCP handshake from the vendor transit at ~MTU 1420, while hosts are currently sending with MSS consistent with 1500. That mismatch will cause stalls and retransmits, especially when NAT reuses ports.
- MSS clamping will prevent hosts from attempting paths with larger segment sizes; it is safe and reversible.
- Increasing ip_local_port_range on the hydra-app fleet from default (32768-60999) to (20000-65535) will reduce collision probability.

Proposed immediate plan (non-disruptive):
1) Push ip_local_port_range change to hydra-app autoscale group (connor — can you coordinate the rollout?)
2) Hydra NetOps to enable NAT gateway ephemeral pool + confirm if nat-gw-eta has any known bugs after the microcode reboot
3) NetOps to enable MSS clamping at the gateway (1360) for the affected VPC for 24 hours and monitor

If the above stabilizes traffic, we'll schedule a maintenance window to expand NAT capacity and then revert MSS clamping if not needed.

—Vivek
Senior Network Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: A. Priya Sharma <priya@hydracloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Hydra Cloud NetOps <netops@hydracloud.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent egress failures from hydra-private-1 VPC (observed 07/13-07/14)

All — quick update after today's changes. We implemented the temporary mitigations at 09:00 UTC (expanded ephemeral pool on nat-gw-eta, ip_local_port_range change on hydra-app ASG, and enabled MSS clamping 1360 on the private gateway). Immediate result: egress timeouts dropped to near-zero for the previously impacted hosts; NAT binding reuse events reduced significantly.

We've opened a follow-up ticket for a durable fix: provisioning a second NAT cluster behind a load-aware front-end to avoid single-cluster port exhaustion. Hydra will schedule that for next sprint; we'll coordinate a maintenance window with you.

Final ask before we close: can Redwood provide a short postmortem (one pager) including: 1) observed failure modes, 2) exact mitigations and timestamps, 3) recommended long-term config changes (dedicated egress IPs, NAT cluster scaling guidance)? If you can drop that into the linked Confluence page and paste the JIRA INF-4829 link, we can attach it to the support ticket.

Thanks for the quick collaboration — Priya
